correctness_confidence.basis: Line-by-line audit of Theorems 1-4, all design-theoretic coprimality and divisibility conditions, Figures 1-3, and edge cases reveals no mathematical errors.

rigor.basis: Proofs are self-contained and clear with explicit analytical vs. asymptotic citations [2, 10], with only minor expository omissions such as not displaying the explicit h3 formula from [9, Thm. 3.4] prior to Theorem 3 and minor legend wording in Fig. 2.

novelty.basis: Strictly advances beyond Liu et al. (arXiv:2611.34386v1) via an unconditional O(1) closed form for z_{w-1}(x), Dual Family B (including non-resolvable BIBDs at l=1 and explicit AG(2,p) open-gap codes), an unconditional TD(q+1,q) t=2 optimal family, and an r=2 non-existence dichotomy, using elementary combinatorial tools.

significance.basis: Meaningfully advances both open problems posed in [9, Sec. 5], though substantial regimes remain open: non-coprime/general t in the open gap, odd w and general n at t=2, and even-t constructions for t>=4.

reproducibility.basis: PDF-only audit cannot inspect external code, but the manuscript clearly documents theorem assumptions, SHA-256 artifact digests, and exact verification boundaries.

summary: This paper proves four sound theorems advancing both open problems of Liu et al. (arXiv:2611.34386v1) for (n,t,w,w-2)-CPECC codes. Theorem 1 gives an unconditional O(1) closed form for z_{w-1}(x) for all w>=4, x>=0. Theorem 2 extends (n,2w-4,1)-RBIBDs into the Frobenius gap under gcd(l,2w-5)=1 and introduces Dual Family B of (n,2w-1,1)-BIBDs/RBIBDs entering the gap for all w>=8 at l=1. Theorem 3 proves a residual-degree jump via Alon-Kahn-Seymour, gives an explicit infinite TD(q+1,q) t=2 optimal family attaining h3, and proves small-u GDD non-existence at t=4. Theorem 4 certifies explicit finite optimal AG(2,p) open-gap codes for prime powers p>=17.
strengths: Theorem 1 gives a clean, complete 5-line proof of the O(1) closed form for z_{w-1}(x) across all w>=4 and x>=0, eliminating the Frobenius threshold restriction of [9, Sec. 4] completely.

Theorem 2's Dual Family B ((n,2w-1,1)-BIBDs at l=1 with no resolvability or coprimality condition, and odd-coprime RBIBDs for l>=2) is a genuinely new optimal construction entering Liu et al.'s open gap for every w>=8, cleanly matched with Family A coprimality conditions.

Theorem 3(1) gives a self-contained double-counting proof via [9, Lemma 3.2] (Alon-Kahn-Seymour) showing that K_{w+2r}-free codewords with Delta<=w+r-2 force |V(G)|>=ceil((2r+1)(w+r-1)/r) and strictly exceed B(w,2r)=(w+r-1)^2 for all w>=2r^2+2, with exact tie at w=2r^2+1.

Theorem 3(2) constructs an explicit, unconditional infinite optimal t=2 family from PG(2,q) minus one point (TD(q+1,q) for odd prime powers q=w+1>=7, zero asymptotic hypothesis) attaining exact equality with h3, and cleanly proves non-existence of small-u paired-group (w+4)-GDDs at r=2 via TD(w+4,w+2) impossibility.

Theorem 4 yields explicit finite optimal codes AG(2,p) inside the open gap for prime powers p=2w-1>=17 (such as AG(2,17) and AG(2,19)), accurately explaining why p in {9,11,13} lie above the threshold and p=15 is non-prime-power.
weaknesses: The mathematical techniques are elementary combinations of classical design existence theorems (Wilson [10], Chang [2], PG(2,q), AG(2,p)) and [9, Lemma 3.2]; no deep new technical machinery is introduced.

Substantial regimes of both open problems remain unresolved: Theorem 2 covers only specific arithmetic progressions in t inside the open gap with asymptotic n (except l=1 AG(2,p)), Theorem 3's t=2 family covers only one sparse length n=(w+1)(w+2) per even w with w+1 an odd prime power, and t>=4 even-t constructions remain open.

The closed-form expression for h3 from [9, Theorem 3.4] is not displayed prior to Theorem 3, being reconstructed only implicitly inside the proof of Theorem 3(2) via the Johnson bound plus residual edge count.
Minor expository mismatch in Figure 2's legend, which labels Family A with (w>=11) and Dual Family B with (w>=8) referring to open-gap entry, while also plotting valid theorem points down to w=5.
strong_novelty_candidates: Unconditional O(1) sawtooth closed form for z_{w-1}(x) eliminating the Frobenius barrier in [9] (Theorem 1).

Dual Family B of (n,2w-1,1)-BIBDs (l=1, entering the open gap for all w>=8 without resolvability) and odd-coprime RBIBDs, plus explicit finite open-gap AG(2,p) codes for prime powers p>=17 (Theorems 2 and 4).

Explicit unconditional infinite t=2 optimal CPECC family from TD(q+1,q) (q=w+1>=7 odd prime power) attaining exact h3 equality, paired with the r=2 (t=4) small-u paired-group GDD non-existence dichotomy and residual-degree jump (Theorem 3).
